title: Aaron Burr to Joseph Alston, New York, [c. 20 July] 1804: stroke-and-figure cipher on the clear page of GLC01523 (catalogue 2049)

documents.shelfmark: Gilder Lehrman Collection, GLC01523 (clear page, lines 15-21)

plaintext.source: No decipherment on the page; Gilder Lehrman calls the cipher undecoded; not in Davis 1837; Kline 1983 lists no July 1804 letter to Alston.

transcription.source: Gilder Lehrman's Hamilton Education Program transcript (stroke signs written as Roman numerals) checked sign by sign against GLC01523_Page_3.png (1200x1400) in 2-3x crops
transcription.notes: The image has two groups in line 19 (II X VII 2 1 VII | 4 1, 'murder be') that the Gilder Lehrman transcript drops. signs.txt is generated from transcription.txt (clear words and the struck word dropped).

system.summary: Simple substitution, one sign per letter: figures 0-8 and 10 for a-l, hatched stroke groups numbered II-X for m-u, three odd signs for v, w, y; words divided, clear words between.
system.notes: Key built in runs: a-f = 5 down to 0, g-i = 6-8, l = 10, m-u = Roman II-X in order. The two number-cipher sheets filed with the letter are a different cipher and date (burr1808).

prior_solution.where: Gilder Lehrman (catalogue, AMDigital, Hamilton Education Program) says undecoded; Davis 1837 does not print the letter; Kline 1983 table of contents lists no letter to Alston in July 1804 (vol. 2 annotation not read); not on cryptiana or DECODE.

conditions.human_role: Project owner pasted the catalogue 2049 contributor task; no target-specific intervention.

solution.what: Hamilton Education Program page: three page PNGs and Gilder Lehrman's transcript PDF.
Gilder Lehrman says undecoded; Davis 1837 prints Burr to Alston 13, 18, 29 July 1804 but not this letter; the 18 July letter names the coroner's jury's object, 'an inquest of murder'.
Simple substitution with word division (21 distinct signs in 132, clear words between).

Pattern words in the sign labels: IX 7 1 = the, IX 7 5 III = than, lambda 7 5 IX = what, II 5 IX 1 VII 8 5 10 VIII = materials, 8 III IX 7 8 VIII VIII IX 5 IX 1 = in this state; every word then reads.
Every sign checked against 2-3x crops of the page; two groups the Gilder Lehrman transcript drops restored in line 19 ('murder be').
'If the inquest of murder be found, what would you advise - To stand - to go to Europe or what?'; one word one sign off ('pleant' for pliant?).
Key structure checked: a-f count down 5-0, g-i up 6-8, m-u Roman II-X; consistent with every occurrence. Content matches Davis's 18 July letter and the inquest timeline.
Kline 1983 table of contents (archive.org search-inside): no letter to Alston in July 1804; cryptiana and DECODE: nothing.

Statistical validation (docs/_validate.py): 132 tokens, 21 types, en-modern order 4: reading -1.897 per letter; random keys -7.513 (z 8.0); key annealed onto shuffled ciphertext best -3.598 (mean -4.058, z 8.7); annealer on the real text -3.741. Verdict: pass.

validation.notes: claimed per-occurrence score -1.897; polyphony 0.0; 0 unread tokens left out; annealer on the real text from random keys reached -3.741

outcome.method_basis: The substitution key was rebuilt from pattern words in the cipher itself; no decipherment, key or plaintext of the passage exists on the page or in print as far as found.
outcome.fraction_read_source: signs.txt and decryption.txt, cipher signs (132), struck word not counted

texts.label: GLC01523, Burr to Joseph Alston, New York, [c. 20 July 1804], clear page lines 15-21
texts.summary: Nine days after the duel with Hamilton, with a coroner's jury sitting to find 'an inquest of murder', Burr tells his son-in-law in cipher that 'the little band', about 20,000 in New York, will stand firm, and asks: if the inquest of murder is found, should he stand trial, go to Europe, or what?

reading_review.note: Every sign reads as sentences; one word one sign off ('pleant' for pliant?).

outcome.notes: Catalogue 2049's 'pp. 2-3 in cipher' are two sheets of a 1808 Vigenere, written up separately as burr1808.
